units.why: The instructor says she drafted the policy with Claude and would use it again, disclosure of the instructor's own AI use (P47).

units.passage: Finally, as far as my own use of AI, I will always share when I have used it on course content.
units.why: 'I will always share when I have used it on course content' (P47).

units.passage: My Usage of Generative AI: Just as I’m asking you not to use Generative AI, I will not use Generative AI to aid in my teaching, grading, or in my communication with you.
units.why: The instructor commits to not using AI 'in my teaching, grading, or in my communication'; a commitment stated to students that limits instructor use (P47).
units.fit_note: A no-use commitment rather than disclosure of actual use; also covers grading (P46). | Also commits the instructor not to use AI for grading, which overlaps P46.

units.passage: My Use of Generative AI: I will model appropriate Generative AI usage by clearly disclosing when I use it and why.
units.why: Instructor commits to 'clearly disclosing when I use it and why'; disclosure of instructor AI use (P47), with modeling (P112) secondary.

units.passage: Instructors are strongly encouraged to identify in a syllabus statement if AI or AI tools will be used to do either or both of the following in the course: Create, augment, or refine instructional materials in a substantial way; Provide initial review of student work, draft feedback, or score materials with a rubric.
units.why: Instructors are 'strongly encouraged to identify in a syllabus statement if AI or AI tools will be used' for materials or for initial review of student work. This is disclosure of instructor AI use to students, P47, modality should.

units.passage: strongly encouraged to disclose to students
units.why: Instructors are 'strongly encouraged to disclose to students in their syllabus statement if they will use' approved AI for review, feedback or scoring. Disclosure of instructor AI use to students: P47.

units.passage: In addition to the required AI policy for your students, you're strongly encouraged to disclose your own AI use on your syllabus. This models transparency and can open the conversation about how AI might be used in your discipline (or not) and why.
units.why: 'you're strongly encouraged to disclose your own AI use on your syllabus' tells instructors to disclose their AI use to students: P47.

units.passage: Any use of voice automation should follow the three recommendations outlined in the Ecampus Voice Automation and AI document. These recommendations emphasize applying professional judgement on a case-by-case basis when deciding to use voice automation and being transparent when it’s employed.
units.why: Voice automation should 'being transparent when it's employed', a disclosure expectation for AI in course media: P47.
units.fit_note: Transparency about AI voice automation in course media, not only disclosure to students of grading or feedback use.

units.passage: Disclose to students when course materials have been created with the use of AI and when AI detection software will be used in the course.
units.why: "and when AI detection software will be used in the course" requires telling students about instructor use of detectors; P47 (disclose instructor AI use) is the nearest, though it concerns detection software.
units.fit_note: Disclosure is about AI detection software used on students rather than instructor use of generative AI. | Discloses use of AI detection software on students rather than instructor use of generative AI.

units.passage: Clearly communicate with students how their data or interactions with AI tools may be used or shared before an instructor puts any of the student’s work into an AI tool, including AI detectors
units.why: Instructors should 'clearly communicate with students how their data or interactions with AI tools may be used or shared before an instructor puts any of the student's work into an AI tool, including AI detectors', which is disclosure of the instructor's own AI use to students (P47).

units.passage: Prof. Lange uses GitHub Copilot for his own daily coding, but he always carefully examines the outputs and takes full responsibility for the final result.
units.why: The instructor says he "uses GitHub Copilot for his own daily coding, but he always carefully examines the outputs", disclosing his own AI use: P47.

units.passage: Instructors should provide a rationale when disclosing their own genAI use in order to build trust and model metacognition, intentionality, and transparency for their students
units.policy: Instructors should provide a rationale when disclosing their own genAI use in order to build trust and model metacognition, intentionality, and transparency for their students.
units.why: 'Instructors should provide a rationale when disclosing their own genAI use' to 'build trust and model metacognition': an instructor-disclosure practice (P47) that adds reasons-giving.
units.fit_note: Adds that the disclosure should carry a rationale to model metacognition and transparency.

units.passage: Instructors shall disclose their own use, if any, of generative AI in grading. 207
units.why: 'Instructors shall disclose their own use, if any, of generative AI in grading' requires telling students about instructor AI use in grading, which is P47 (not P46, since it does not say who assigns grades).

units.passage: It is also important to include the use of these tools in any discussion with students around course policies, making clear why and how such services may be used in the course.
units.why: Instructors should 'include the use of these tools in any discussion with students around course policies'; telling students how detectors are used, P47.
units.fit_note: Disclosure concerns instructors' use of detectors, not of AI itself. Specifically asks instructors to tell students if and how detectors may be used.

units.passage: Just as students are obligated to acknowledge their use of AI, instructors should also be transparent about their use of AI tools in their design of course activities.
units.why: 'Instructors should also be transparent about their use of AI tools in their design of course activities' requires instructors to disclose their own use; P47 fits.

units.passage: as well as a disclosure statement if AI is used for other pedagogical aspects such as assignment building or grading.
units.why: Instructors who use AI for 'assignment building or grading' should add 'a disclosure statement'; this is instructor disclosure to students (P47), not student disclosure.

units.passage: If AI was used to develop course materials, create assessments, or generate feedback, faculty should be forthcoming and prepared to discuss the rationale, scope, and implications of its use.
units.why: Principle 3 says faculty "should be forthcoming and prepared to discuss the rationale, scope, and implications" of using AI for materials, assessments or feedback; disclosure of instructor AI use to students is P47 (materials also touch P48, but the duty is to be transparent).
units.fit_note: Covers AI used for course materials, assessments and feedback.

units.passage: Transparency of this sort fosters trust and helps reinforce community norms about AI use.
units.why: 'Transparency of this sort fosters trust and helps reinforce community norms about AI use' gives the reason for instructor disclosure; kept under P47 as its rationale.
units.fit_note: States the rationale (trust, community norms) for instructor transparency rather than the duty itself.

units.passage: Be transparent where appropriate
units.why: "When faculty use AI in teaching materials, research or professional work: Be transparent where appropriate." Faculty disclosure of their own AI use, so P47.
units.fit_note: Transparency is not tied to students and is limited to where appropriate; covers research and professional work too.

units.passage: Consider disclosing GenAI use to students to model transparency in the teaching and learning process.
units.why: "Consider disclosing GenAI use to students to model transparency" recommends instructors disclose their AI use, P47.

units.passage: When instructors prohibit student use of AI but rely on it themselves, particularly without transparency, it can create confusion, erode trust, and undermine the values of academic integrity.
units.why: "When instructors prohibit student use of AI but rely on it themselves" names an inconsistency that "erode[s] trust", an argument for instructor transparency, P47.

units.passage: If AI is used to enhance course development, assignment design, or feedback, it is advisable to be transparent with students by noting in the syllabus that “elements of this course have been optimized with GenAI” and providing any additional details as needed.
units.why: "it is advisable to be transparent with students by noting in the syllabus" that course elements "have been optimized with GenAI" recommends disclosure of instructor AI use, P47.

units.passage: Some assignments may be graded using AI tools
units.why: "Some assignments may be graded using AI tools" that assess multiple-choice and provide initial essay feedback; tells students AI grading may occur, nearest P47.
units.fit_note: States that AI grading may occur; no commitment to disclose or limit it. | States that AI grading may occur but sets no conditions.

units.passage: Inform students when AI tools are being used in the course and how
units.why: "Inform students when AI tools are being used in the course and how they will impact learning and assessment"; instructor disclosure, P47.

units.passage: To model best practices for your students, always disclose your approach to AI integration, the factors considered when evaluating AI-generated Using Generative AI in Teaching, Learning and Research January 2025 | Page 4 content, and your rationale for adopting it.
units.why: "always disclose your approach to AI integration, the factors considered ... and your rationale" is an instructor duty to disclose to students, so P47.
units.fit_note: Disclosure covers the approach and rationale for adopting AI, not only the instructor's own use.

units.passage: Faculty should consider disclosing or citing their own AI use.
units.why: 'Faculty should consider disclosing or citing their own AI use' asks instructors to tell students about their AI use, P47 (should).

units.passage: I do not use generative AI to evaluate or grade student work
units.why: 'I do not use generative AI to evaluate or grade student work' is a commitment limiting instructor AI use and disclosed to students, P47 (commit to limits).

units.passage: faculty should disclose any AI grading practices with students
units.why: 'At a minimum, faculty should disclose any AI grading practices with students' requires telling students about AI grading, P47.

units.passage: faculty should disclose any AI grading practices with students
units.why: 'At a minimum, faculty should disclose any AI grading practices with students' requires telling students about AI grading, P47.

units.passage: This document was edited for grammar using Grammarly, an AI tool for writing.
units.why: "This document was edited for grammar using Grammarly, an AI tool for writing" discloses the office's own AI use; P47 is nearest.
units.fit_note: Discloses AI use by the office that wrote the page, not by an instructor to students.

units.passage: You will be informed about what data (if any) is shared, provided, or stored when we use any AI tool in the classroom—and you can opt out.
units.why: "You will be informed about what data (if any) is shared, provided, or stored when we use any AI tool in the classroom" commits instructors to tell students about their AI tool use; P47 (disclose instructor AI use).
units.fit_note: Disclosure concerns data shared with AI tools used in class, not only grading or feedback. Disclosure concerns data handling in instructor AI use, not grading or feedback methods.

units.passage: students should disclose AI use according to course expectations and consult instructors when uncertain; instructors using AI to generate feedback, to grade, or who upload student work to AI tools or detectors should disclose these uses to students; researchers should follow disciplinary norms and publisher policies; and all members of the Tufts community should abide by their respective school, department, and unit policies.
units.why: Instructors who use AI for feedback or grading, or upload student work to tools or detectors, "should disclose these uses to students", P47.

units.passage: Students must be informed that AI tools are being used in grading.
units.why: 'Students must be informed that AI tools are being used in grading' requires instructors to tell students if AI is used in grading: P47.

units.passage: If you are planning to use AI to help provide feedback for grading, inform students that you will be using AI for that purpose and reassure them that you will be reviewing the feedback.
units.why: 'If you are planning to use AI to help provide feedback for grading, inform students that you will be using AI' and review the feedback: P47 (disclose instructor AI use).

units.passage: To establish best practices regarding use of Gen AI, faculty should consider citing/acknowledging their own use of AI when used in their courses.
units.why: "faculty should consider citing/acknowledging their own use of AI when used in their courses" asks instructors to disclose their own AI use, so P47.

units.passage: Faculty evaluation: May need AI use disclosure considerations
units.why: 'Faculty evaluation: May need AI use disclosure considerations'; an item on instructor AI disclosure for review, P47.
units.fit_note: A flagged item for future review, not a rule.

units.passage: Just as you may expect students to be transparent with you about their use of generative AI, be prepared to share with students how you are using it
units.why: 'be prepared to share with students how you are using it' asks instructors to disclose their own AI use (P47).
